dedupe_keys.name: hhs empower map and emergency planning de identified dataset electricity dependent medicare beneficiaries

description: The HHS emPOWER Program gives emergency planners data on people who depend on electricity for their health. Its public map shows, for each state, territory, county and ZIP Code, the number of Medicare beneficiaries and how many have had claims for electricity-dependent medical equipment such as ventilators and oxygen concentrators, or rely on essential services such as dialysis, oxygen, home health or hospice at home, with combinations of the two, over near real-time natural hazard layers; selected results can be downloaded. The monthly Emergency Planning De-identified Dataset gives the same totals to public health authorities. The producers are the Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response and the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services; the programme covers more than 4.6 million such beneficiaries. Coverage is the United States and its territories, updated monthly, with the planning dataset available since 2014. The map and a REST service are free to view; the full planning dataset is restricted to state, territorial and major metropolitan preparedness programmes. Caveats: only Medicare beneficiaries are counted (a Medicaid pilot is separate), counts are aggregated and small cells may be suppressed, and claims lag actual equipment use. Simulation uses: estimating health impacts of power outages and cascading failures from electricity to healthcare, prioritising restoration and welfare checks, and exposure of vulnerable residents to storms, heat and wildfire shutoffs. Related records: HIFLD Open (data-hifld-open) gives facility and grid layers.
